detailed_description:
Angular stylised 3D animation, brush-stroke texture, Horsell, Surrey, 1894, low sun from the left, black shadows.
[Shot 1] From 00:00 to 00:08. The shot opens on a medium close shot of <Subject 1>'s face above the rim of the cylinder: two immense glossy black eyes set wide apart in the wet grey-brown hide, below them the quivering V-shaped lipless mouth with its pointed upper lip, and the whip tentacles hanging in two bunches on either side of it. The camera is on the near lip of the pit looking down at the lower rim of the aperture, a 300mm lens. The low sun comes from the LEFT. At the first frame the Martian's face fills the CENTRE of the frame, the bulk half the frame's height and about four feet across. The shot is inside this place: The great raw crater on Horsell Common with the sun going down in 1894: walls of loose yellow sand and grey gravel dug back and scored by spades, a charred rim of blackened turf heaped with spoil, planks and pickaxes on the gravel floor, a broken length of new white railing trodden flat into the sand along the near lip. The camera keeps a static shot on <Subject 1>'s face, keeping the two black eyes in the upper centre of frame as the lipless mouth opens under the eyes, pants against the strange air and the wedge of the lower lip drives down, and a thread of saliva swings off its brim and runs onto the metal with the two black eyes on the lens, from 00:00 to 00:04. At 00:04 the whole bulk heaves once with the breath and the two bunches of tentacles sway across the wet hide, and the movement continues to the last frame of the shot. <Subject 1>'s mouth is closed from 00:00 to 00:05 while the lipless mouth opens under the eyes. By 00:08 the camera is keeping through the last frame, and the action continues with it.
